rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John’s miraculous birth from an elderly father and infertile mother undermines the claim that a miraculous birth proves Jesus’ divinity; John claimed no divinity and was not made a god by others.
rows.anchor: if a mere miraculous birth is enough to prove the divinity of Jesus (sws), then this proof is also present in favour of John (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recounts Mary’s pure life and Jesus’ birth, then stresses Jesus’ declaration that he is God’s servant, charged with prayer and zakāh, rebuking those who make him God’s peer and Mary the mother of God’s son.
rows.anchor: in his cradle proclaimed himself to be a servant of God and being given the directives of the prayer and zakāh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christians are rebuked for disputing about Jesus despite his clear teaching and warned that the disputes will be settled on an approaching day.
rows.anchor: Christians are rebuked on their mutual differences regarding Jesus (sws) in spite of the latter’s clear teachings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s invitation to his father to worship one God led to migration, which God rewarded with children despite Abraham’s old age.
rows.anchor: the way Abraham (sws) invited his father to monotheism and the way he had to migrate as a result

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The steadfast prophets Moses, Aaron, Ishmael, and Idrīs came through earlier prophetic lineages and prostrated at God’s revelations; later descendants abandoned prayer, zakāh, and obedience to God, but repentant reformers can be saved.
rows.anchor: These were very steadfast prophets among the progeny of Adam (sws), Noah (sws), Abraham (sws) and Jacob (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel’s speech urges the Prophet to wait steadfastly for God’s decree and not hurry.
rows.anchor: Through the tongue of Gabriel, the Prophet (sws) is directed to be patient and wait for the decree of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny the Hereafter are rebuked and warned about their fate.
rows.anchor: Those who deny the Hereafter are rebuked and admonished and their fate is pointed out

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy opponents wrongly infer from their worldly status that their beliefs and deeds are superior, deny the Judgment, and assume they would remain better off if it came; God refutes this reasoning.
rows.anchor: They contended that if they were well-off in relation to the believers of the Qur’ān, it necessarily means that their beliefs and deeds were also better

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should patiently disregard demands to hasten punishment, depend on the Qur’an to warn and give glad tidings, and tell stubborn people the fate they will meet if they persist.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is urged to be patient and wait: he should not be worried at the demand of those who want to hasten the punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing passage first calls the Prophet to steadfastness, rebukes deniers of Judgment and their worldly-status argument, then directs him to warn and give glad tidings through the Qur’an and explain the fate of the obdurate.
rows.anchor: First, through the tongue of Gabriel, the Prophet (sws) is urged to be steadfast. After that, the rejecters of the Day of Judgement are rebuked.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters think their superior worldly rank proves they are more guided and expect their status to continue after death through intercessors and partners of God.
rows.anchor: they regard themselves to be more guided and if ever there is going to be a Judgement Day they will have this same status through the help of their intercessors and partners of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an supplies suitable guidance for each phase of delivering the truth; the Prophet must warn stubborn people of the fate awaiting them if they persist.
rows.anchor: he must depend on the Qur’ ān for this purpose as it has appropriate guidance for them in every phase of delivering the truth to them

none: This segment gives only the translated text of verses 19:64-76, with no separate commentary point.
This segment gives only the translated text of verses 19:77-85, with no separate commentary point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel’s words urge patience and clarify that he and the angels have no independent agency: they only follow God’s commands.
rows.anchor: God’s directives. There is a special background to this advice and explanation given by him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because revelation is the Prophet’s support in conflict, he naturally awaits Gabriel anxiously; like a soldier awaiting guidance, he must wait for help at its appointed time, as Qur’anic instruction elsewhere also teaches.
rows.anchor: the sole support for the Prophet (sws) against his opponents in this phase of conflict with his opponents was divine revelation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel effectively apologizes that angels descend and bring revelation only at God’s command, so delay is not their fault and they cannot act independently.
rows.anchor: Gabriel has actually presented a type of apology to the Prophet (sws) that his coming with divine revelation is based on God’s command

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ total subordination rebuts Arab polytheists who worshipped them as God’s daughters and expected their intercession; if even Gabriel is powerless, other angels have still less power.
rows.anchor: the reason for explaining this status of the angels was to refute the notion of the Arab polytheists who worshipped angels

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance that the Lord forgets nothing comforts the Prophet that no angel can exploit a lapse in awareness to carry out a plan independently.
rows.anchor: God is not forgetful that anyone of them can use this forgetfulness to his advantage and implement his own will

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final question may be Gabriel’s speech or a divine insertion, but the meaning is unchanged; Islahi prefers that Gabriel is speaking because the Prophet is watched over by the Lord of all creation.
rows.anchor: My own inclination is towards the first probability. It is Gabriel who urged the Prophet (sws) to wait and exercise patience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship here has its wider sense of obedience, as it does in 19:44.
rows.anchor: here worhsip is used in its wider connotation and also includes obedience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic form of the word for perseverance magnifies the meaning; with the preposition lām, it also conveys waiting, nuances difficult to preserve in translation.
rows.anchor: It has a greater amount of stress in it. It should be kept in mind that increase in letters of a word magnifies its meaning too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God has no peer, no one can thwart his intentions; the Prophet should continue his work and God will ease his hardships and accomplish his purposes.
rows.anchor: when there is no peer or match of God, who can hinder His intentions to materialize

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel’s speech ends and God begins speaking, naming the adversaries’ real reason for denial before refuting it; the general ‘man’ refers contextually to Arabian idolaters and expresses contempt.
rows.anchor: Gabriel’s words end here and it is now the Almighty Who begins His speech

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab idolaters did not consistently deny Judgment: they believed God gives life and death but found resurrection after death improbable, while the wealthy expected to retain their status and trusted their deities.
rows.anchor: They held contradictory views about it. They believed that God gives life and death but regarded it to be farfetched

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters called deities God’s daughters and expected them to exempt their worshippers from judgment; remembering this contradiction clarifies the following Qur’anic discussion.
rows.anchor: the Day comes, these deities will exempt them from accountability

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the idolaters accept that God first created humanity from nothing, they have no reason to find its re-creation from something impossible.
rows.anchor: when they cannot deny that God has created mankind from nothingness, why do regard being created again as something far-fetched

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Devils’ includes both jinn and human tempters: Arabs worshipped jinn, followed their deviant leaders blindly, and harassed the messenger when he called them to see clearly.
rows.anchor: the word “devils” here encompasses both devils among men and the jinn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term for sitting on one’s knees describes criminals awaiting a ruler’s verdict; here they wait to learn which part of Hell they will enter, under an oath’s emphasis.
rows.anchor: This is the sitting position of criminals – just as criminals sit before a ruler to hear his verdict

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most rebellious leaders will be separated from their followers so they can lead them to Hell as they led them astray in worldly life; each will enter a deserved division.
rows.anchor: The purpose would be to make them lead their followers to Hell just as they led them astray in the previous world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows who deserves each part of Hell, a sarcastic rebuttal to the idolaters’ intercession theory: an intercessor would have to claim superior knowledge of a person’s piety.
rows.anchor: This is a subtle sarcasm on the wrong belief of intercession held by the idolaters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ḥatm means incumbent; shifting from indirect reference to direct address expresses anger, so God directly orders the wrongdoers into Hell and assures the Prophet this fixed judgment will occur.
rows.anchor: Since the purpose is to express immense anger for these wrongdoers, God will directly address them and order them to enter Hell without any exception

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects commentators’ view that everyone, righteous and wicked, must pass through Hell and that the righteous escape by crossing a bridge; the style and 21:101–103 instead keep the righteous away from it.
rows.anchor: our exegetes have regarded this verse to address all mankind. Thus they regard everyone whether, pious or wrongdoer to pass through Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misunderstandings of Qur’anic style cause many interpretive errors.
rows.anchor: most erroneous interpretations are the result of such misunderstandings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks sequence: God deals with wrongdoers first, then turns to those who fear him.
rows.anchor: God will first deal with the wrongdoers. After consigning them to Hell, He will turn to those who feared Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saving the God-fearing means relieving their anxieties and wait before their final destination, not rescuing them from Hell, whose sound they will not hear.
rows.anchor: Saving the God-fearing here does not mean saving them from Hell because they will not even hear its sound

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the knee-sitting term clearly describes wrongdoers in 19:68, here it means they await transfer to Hell’s keepers and opening of its gates; Islahi rejects exegetes’ lexically strained reading that they are already in Hell.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, here this word is used for the situation when after God’s judgement they will be consigned to the keepers of Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers argue that their superior worldly status proves God favors them more than believers and so they should not expect divine wrath or punishment.
rows.anchor: since in this world they have a superior status, why should they think that they deserve the wrath of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic word qarn can mean either the people of one era or a nation.
rows.anchor: The word Q refers to “people of one era” as well as to a “nation.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material wealth, resources, and splendour do not indicate divine favour or protect a nation from God’s grasp; destroyed earlier peoples demonstrate this.
rows.anchor: things save it from God’s grasp. The fate of previous nations bears witness to this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established practice is to grant defiant, wealthy opponents respite until promised worldly punishment or the Judgment; delayed punishment reflects secure planning, not weakness.
rows.anchor: He keeps giving respite until either the punishment that is ordained to visit those who deny their messenger visits them or the Day of Judgment appears

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording presents respite as what the Most Merciful’s power, wisdom, and planning require; the unfortunate mistake this delay for success and grow more rebellious.
rows.anchor: giving respite to the wrongdoers is a requisite of God’s power, wisdom and planning

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When paired, ‘the punishment’ means punishment in this world and ‘the Hour’ means punishment in the next; messengers warn of both, and a people denying their messenger after truth is conclusive are destroyed.
rows.anchor: When both these are stated together, the first refers to worldly punishment and the second to the next-worldly punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic sometimes uses a superlative without making a comparison.
rows.anchor: superlatives are at times used without comparison

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy with modern scientific arrogance, Islahi recounts a claim that Americans live longer than people in the subcontinent and answers that suicide rates are also higher, so people still cannot escape death.
rows.anchor: not only their average age is more but the suicide rate is also more

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 76 parallels the previous verse: God increases guidance for those choosing guidance, while sensible people value lasting consequences over immediate gains.
rows.anchor: just as God gives respite to those who give preference to deviance over guidance, in the same way, He continues to give more guidance to people who adopt guidance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures believers that increasing guidance and good deeds secure their eternal afterlife, while opponents’ worldly wealth will become fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: their guidance is increasing by the day and what they are gathering in the form of good deeds is guaranteeing the eternal kingdom of God for them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi translates maraddan as ‘consequence,’ judging that rendering close to the word’s essence.
rows.anchor: as consequence and his translation is very close to the real essence of the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘lasting righteous deeds’ implies that only actions enduring beyond worldly life are truly righteous; deeds done solely for God and the Hereafter endure because God and the Hereafter are eternal.
rows.anchor: Eternal deeds are only those which are done solely for God and the Hereafter because God is eternal and so is the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic opening a-fa-ra’ayta signals a delusion of grandeur or foolishness when introducing the disbeliever’s boast.
rows.anchor: when the address begins with this word, then it means that a person who has delusions of grandeur about himself or something very foolish is being referred to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic alladhi need not introduce a definite, named person; it can introduce a similitude, as in 16:92, and here depicts a group's mentality.
rows.anchor: At times, it also occurs for a similitude, some very eloquent examples of which are found in the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mentality depicted treats blessings as entitlement or personal competence, assumes a birthright to wealth and leadership, and expects to enjoy the same in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: They regard themselves to be entitled to them or think that they are the consequence of their own competence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the boast is foolish and childish, the Qur’an answers it sarcastically and disparagingly.
rows.anchor: Since this claim is totally foolish and childish too, it is answered in a sarcastic and disparaging way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response rejects the boast furiously: disbelief brings punishment that increases for arrogance, and on Judgment Day the claimant loses all God-given possessions and appears alone and empty-handed.
rows.anchor: On the Day of Judgement, such a person will have no helpers or their deities or intercessors to save him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters especially trusted angels’ intercession because they regarded angels as God’s favoured daughters who provided worldly sustenance and children and would help after death; their alleged support has no power to save them.
rows.anchor: they greatly trusted the intercession of the angels for they regarded them to be favoured daughters of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word used for the deities’ backing means power and strength.
rows.anchor: Its actual meaning is “power and strength.”
